wave: CENSUS BLINDNESS -- empirically cross-check the Cargo dependency census against this workspace's own real Cargo.toml files, rather than reading census code in isolation
wave_title: Continuing this cycle's recensus with a genuinely different method after two code-reading-based checks (arm completeness, sub-field completeness): actually RAN census_cargo_workspace against this repository's own real root and manually cross-checked every direct workspace-member edge it produced against each Cargo.toml file's own [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies] tables, rather than trusting the parser's own code to prove its own correctness.
priority_classification: census blindness -- the next tier in the standing priority order after correctness/architectural-integrity and security, both already covered this cycle. A dependency census that silently misses or misclassifies a real edge in Atlas's own self-census is exactly the kind of blind spot this priority tier names.
method: wrote a throwaway `cargo run --example` harness (deleted after recording this finding, matching the established precedent for out-of-band empirical probes this session) calling adapter::dependency::cargo::census_cargo_workspace(Path::new(".")) against this repository's actual root, then manually read all four workspace members' real Cargo.toml files (core, adapter, runtime, apps/cli) and checked every single dependency line against the tool's own output.

findings.top_level_report_fields: state=Closed, dangling_references=[], unsupported_constructs=[] -- a fully clean parse of this repository's real Cargo.lock/manifests, no malformed-lockfile or unparsed-construct signal.
edge_by_edge_cross_check: core/Cargo.toml declares exactly [serde] -> census reports core -> serde (Runtime, Registry). Match.

adapter/Cargo.toml declares [atlas_core(path)/serde/syn/quote/proc-macro2] plus [dev-dependencies: serde_json] -> census reports all 5 runtime edges as Runtime AND adapter -> serde_json specifically as Dev (correctly distinguishing the [dev-dependencies] table from [dependencies], the exact role/table distinction this module's own doc comment calls out as previously broken by an earlier design that collapsed role with optional/target-conditional facts). Match, including the one subtle case that would be easy to get wrong.

runtime/Cargo.toml declares [atlas_core(path)/adapter(path)/serde_json] -> census reports all 3 as Runtime, with core/adapter correctly marked WorkspaceMember (path dependencies to sibling workspace crates) rather than Registry. Match.
apps/cli/Cargo.toml (package name atlas-cli) declares [runtime(path)/serde/serde_json] -> census reports all 3 as Runtime, runtime correctly marked WorkspaceMember. Match.
findings.conclusion: All 13 direct workspace-member edges present in the census output; zero edges present in a real Cargo.toml but absent from the census output; zero edges present in the census output but absent from a real Cargo.toml; the one role-classification subtlety this module's own history flags as previously broken (Dev vs Runtime, independent of optional/target-conditional) is correctly handled for the one real case in this workspace that exercises it (adapter's serde_json).
